decisions.reason: The Hero V was already approved and locked, and its existing message-160 MODIFY captures the newly explicit requirement to carry it forward unchanged unless the client requests a change.
The existing message-160 MODIFY already records that complete-wordmark exploration must occur around the locked Hero V, second V, and É accent.
The existing message-160 MODIFY already records both the É accent's locked-asset status and its carry-forward-without-change policy.
The existing message-160 MODIFY already constrains letterform exploration to occur around the three locked assets while preserving them unchanged.
Locking the approved second V does not itself alter or cancel the established terminal-treatment rules; the source supplies no new terminal geometry or shared-terminal decision.
The asset-lock decision concerns geometry preservation and does not change the deferred champagne-metal material treatment or its application sequence.
Preserving the approved second V does not change the brand's expression, positioning, visual-tone, or symbolism requirements.
The second V asset-lock decision leaves unchanged the requirement for a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
Locking the second V does not modify the final production-ready artwork deliverable or its delivery scope.
